From a2567217ade970ecc458144b6be469bc015b23e5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Keenan Dong <keenanat2000@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Apr 2026 13:12:41 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] rxrpc: fix oversized RESPONSE authenticator length check

rxgk_verify_response() decodes auth_len from the packet and is supposed
to verify that it fits in the remaining bytes. The existing check is
inverted, so oversized RESPONSE authenticators are accepted and passed
to rxgk_decrypt_skb(), which can later reach skb_to_sgvec() with an
impossible length and hit BUG_ON(len).

Decoded from the original latest-net reproduction logs with
scripts/decode_stacktrace.sh:

RIP: __skb_to_sgvec()
  [net/core/skbuff.c:5285 (discriminator 1)]
Call Trace:
 skb_to_sgvec() [net/core/skbuff.c:5305]
 rxgk_decrypt_skb() [net/rxrpc/rxgk_common.h:81]
 rxgk_verify_response() [net/rxrpc/rxgk.c:1268]
 rxrpc_process_connection()
   [net/rxrpc/conn_event.c:266 net/rxrpc/conn_event.c:364
    net/rxrpc/conn_event.c:386]
 process_one_work() [kernel/workqueue.c:3281]
 worker_thread()
   [kernel/workqueue.c:3353 kernel/workqueue.c:3440]
 kthread() [kernel/kthread.c:436]
 ret_from_fork() [arch/x86/kernel/process.c:164]

Reject authenticator lengths that exceed the remaining packet payload.

Fixes: 9d1d2b59341f ("rxrpc: rxgk: Implement the yfs-rxgk security class (GSSAPI)")
Signed-off-by: Keenan Dong <keenanat2000@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
cc: Marc Dionne <marc.dionne@auristor.com>
cc: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
cc: Willy Tarreau <w@1wt.eu>
cc: linux-afs@lists.infradead.org
cc: stable@kernel.org
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260408121252.2249051-14-dhowells@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/net/rxrpc/rxgk.c b/net/rxrpc/rxgk.c
index 01dbdf0b5cf2..9e4a4ff28913 100644
--- a/net/rxrpc/rxgk.c
+++ b/net/rxrpc/rxgk.c
@@ -1224,7 +1224,7 @@ static int rxgk_verify_response(struct rxrpc_connection *conn,
 
 	auth_offset	= offset;
 	auth_len	= ntohl(xauth_len);
-	if (auth_len < len)
+	if (auth_len > len)
 		goto short_packet;
 	if (auth_len & 3)
 		goto inconsistent;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

The patch contains a single-file change in `net/rxrpc/rxgk.c` that fixes an inverted length check for the authenticator in a `RESPONSE` packet.

### Modifications in each file

1. **net/rxrpc/rxgk.c**  
   - Changed the condition `if (auth_len < len)` to `if (auth_len > len)` in function `rxgk_verify_response()`.  
   - This corrects the validation of the authenticator length (`auth_len`) against the remaining payload bytes (`len`). The original code incorrectly accepted oversized authenticators (when `auth_len` exceeded `len`) and rejected valid ones.

### Relationships

- The single-line change directly fixes a bug where an inverted comparison allowed oversized RESPONSE authenticators to pass validation. This could later trigger a `BUG_ON(len)` in `__skb_to_sgvec()` when `rxgk_decrypt_skb()` attempted to build a scatter-gather list with an impossible length. The correction ensures that only authenticator lengths that fit within the remaining packet payload are accepted, preventing the crash.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
if (auth_len < len)
Reason:
The condition is inverted: it accepts oversized authenticator lengths (when auth_len is larger than the remaining packet length) because the check passes if auth_len is less than len. This allows a malicious or malformed packet to pass the length validation, leading to an impossible length being passed to `skb_to_sgvec()` via `rxgk_decrypt_skb()`, which then hits `BUG_ON(len)`.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (auth_len > len)
Reason:
The corrected condition correctly rejects oversized authenticators by failing the check when `auth_len` exceeds the remaining packet payload (`len`). This ensures that only authenticators that fit within the packet are accepted, preventing the impossible length from reaching the vulnerability in `skb_to_sgvec()`.
